edges.effect_quant: Colorectal-cancer syntheses consistently place higher whole-grain intake on the lower-risk side, with the signal usually modest rather than dramatic.
edges.mechanism: Whole grains deliver fiber, resistant starch, and a different glycemic profile than refined grains, all of which can shift colonic fermentation and reduce exposure to pro-carcinogenic metabolic conditions. The protection signal is therefore mechanistically plausible and not just a dietary-pattern proxy, even though healthy-user bias remains possible.
edges.summary: The strongest direct synthesis found lower colorectal-cancer risk in people eating more whole grains and other favorable food groups. Later umbrella reviews did not overturn that finding; instead, they kept whole grains on the more credible protective side of the diet-and-colorectal-cancer literature.
edges.caveats: Whole-grain intake travels with many other healthy behaviors, so observational confounding is unavoidable. The evidence is strongest for habitual dietary patterns over time, not for a short-term dietary add-on.

evidence.citation: Schwingshackl L et al 2018 Int J Cancer
